html:
Manila is the capital of the Philippines, on Manila Bay in the west of Luzon. Before the Spanish came it was Maynila, a walled trading town under Muslim rulers, with ties to Brunei and trade with China.

The Spanish under Miguel López de Legazpi took it in 1571 and made it the capital of their colony. They built the walled city of Intramuros, with churches, convents and the University of Santo Tomas of 1611. One of the first books printed in the islands, the Doctrina Christiana, came from Manila in 1593.

For 250 years the Manila galleons linked it to Acapulco in Mexico, trading Mexican silver for Chinese silk and porcelain. That made it one of the first hubs of a truly global trade. A large Chinese merchant community lived just outside the walls, needed by the Spanish but also feared, and several times massacred.

Britain held the city in 1762 to 1764. The Spanish shot the writer José Rizal there in 1896, which fed the revolution. In 1898 the United States took the islands. In the Battle of Manila in 1945, between American and Japanese forces, much of the city was destroyed and some 100,000 civilians died.
sum: Manila is the capital of the Philippines, on Manila Bay in the west of Luzon. Before the Spanish came it was Maynila, a walled trading town under Muslim rulers, with ties to Brunei and trade with China.
